title: texture wrap (CLAMP_TO_EDGE vs REPEAT) + NEAREST filter oracle
purpose: 8-cell 4x2 grid sampling a 4x4 quadrant texture (TL=RED, TR=GREEN, BL=BLUE, BR=WHITE in 2x2 quadrants of texels). All vertices in each cell share the SAME UV so smooth interpolation yields constant UV; NEAREST filter then picks one texel deterministically. NV2A LU_IMAGE_ textures use TEXEL-UNIT (unnormalized) UV coordinates -- Row 0 uses wrap=CLAMP_TO_EDGE with in-range UVs (0.5/2.5 = midpoints of texel columns 0/2) hitting each of the 4 quadrants directly. Row 1 uses wrap=REPEAT (NV097 ADDRESS U/V = 1) with UVs offset by +TEX_W=+4 in U; if WRAP works, the offset wraps back to the row-0 sample positions, producing the SAME R/G/B/W pattern. If WRAP is mis-implemented (e.g. silently treated as CLAMP_TO_EDGE), row 1 would clamp to U=3.5 = texel col 3 (GREEN/WHITE) exposing the bug. The §4.11 spec also calls for LINEAR filter + 4 additional wrap modes (MIRROR, CLAMP, BORDER, plus CYLINDER variants); v0.1 narrows to NEAREST + CLAMP_TO_EDGE + REPEAT to keep the output byte-exact (LINEAR produces sub-texel fractional outputs that need compare_overrides tolerance). Builds on the xbed_lib texture infrastructure (xbed_texture_bind_stage0 + xbed_load_textured_shaders) shipped same session. **2026-05-20 late evening: GREEN on Metal after v0.1 UV-scale fix.** Initial run was EXPECTED_FAIL due to test-author confusion about UV scale (used normalized [0..1] instead of texel-unit [0..TEX_W]); the renderer's PSH norm0() divides by texSize per the NV2A texture-shader contract (matches the nxdk mesh sample's UV convention with integer pixel coords). Renamed task #15 from "Metal TEX0 propagation" to "texture-filter-wrap UV scale fix" and closed. Real Xbox + GL renderer expected to PASS.
